newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends slightly higher on buy-backs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends slightly higher on buy-backs.

text.p: The key December three-month euroyen futures contract ended slightly higher on Thursday on short-covering after the previous day's sharp falls, but the upside was limited, traders said.
"The upside is heavy due to concern about higher interest rates and the yen's weakness against the dollar (on Thursday)," a city bank trader said.
The December's day session turnover was 51,244 contracts.
On Wednesday, euroyen futures fell sharply on a report that quoted the deputy governor of the Bank of Japan (BOJ) as saying the BOJ was considering the appropriate timing for a credit tightening.
A senior BOJ official later denied the report and said the BOJ has no plans to raise rates immediately.

"Although the deputy governor's comments were later denied by the BOJ, the fact that such comments came out in the first place may be an indication that the BOJ is starting to pave the way (towards raising interest rates)," the city bank trader said.
The trader said the December was likely to move in a range of around 98.82 to 98.99 in the near term.
Others said, however, that fears of an interest rate rise were not very strong at this point.

"Some market players may be starting to factor in a possible rise in interest rates...(but) I don't think the market's fears of higher interest rates are all that acute at this point," a trader for a major brokerage house said.
Concern about interest rates is unlikely to overwhelm the market until such fears are backed up by solid evidence in the form of strong economic indicators, the trader said.

The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) said on Thursday that its London branch made a 10 billion yen loss as of April 1 from derivatives trading, but this news had little impact on euroyen futures, traders said.

"If anything, this is a buy factor, as it can lead to concern about Japan's financial system, but it had little effect. I suppose the market felt that the amount of the loss was too small," the city bank trader said.
The Bank of Japan injected a net 200 billion yen into the money market on Thursday morning, almost totally offsetting a projected fund shortage of 190 billion yen.
Traders said the weighted average of the key overnight call rate was likely to be 0.50 percent on Thursday, up from the previous day's 0.48 percent.
About 10 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.58 percent.
About 20 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were issued at 0.56 percent.

In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, long-term rates fell due to a rise in JGBs and the yield curve flattened somewhat, traders said. The 10-year IRS rate was quoted at 3.00/04 percent, down from Wednesday's 3.04/08 percent.
